title: Can Independent Auditors Detect Sandbagging? A Small-Scale Replication of the Auditing Game

original_idea.body:
# Can Independent Auditors Detect Sandbagging? A Small-Scale Replication of the Auditing Game

**Problem:** An auditing-game study found teams could not reliably distinguish sandbagging from benign models; it used a controlled setup not re-run cheaply by outsiders.

**Direction:** Construct a minimal sandbagging organism on an open model, run a black-box auditor protocol (consistency checks, elicitation, refusal-pattern analysis), measure detection rate and which signals survive.

**Why it matters:** Sandbagging breaks evaluation-based governance; whether resource-limited auditors can detect it is counterfactually valuable.

**Relevant context:** Extends arXiv:2512.07810 and arXiv:2406.07358.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: whether external auditors can detect sandbagging directly bears on eval-based governance, a critical pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt-based sandbagging organism + black-box auditor protocol on an open model; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused detection-rate replication; organism setup adds a dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected long-horizon threat labs have no incentive to answer; open model, no training.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-based auditing on an open model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The auditing-game result exists; a cheap open-model replication is the open extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The result exists; the cheap outsider replication is the open extension.
